## 1. About webR and this example

### What is webR?

[webR](https://docs.r-wasm.org/webr/latest/) is a version of the R interpreter
compiled to WebAssembly, that runs entirely in the web browser — no server, no
installation, no R setup required. It allows to run R code, load packages, and
create graphics interactively on any device with a modern browser. Packages are
provided as pre-compiled WebAssembly binaries from the
[r-wasm package repository](https://repo.r-wasm.org/).

### The example

This example demonstrates that **deSolve**, a package for numerical solution of
differential equation models, now runs in webR as well. It simulates the
classic Lorenz system — a benchmark example of deterministic chaos — and
visualizes the result as time series and in a 3-dimensional phase space plot.

## 2. How to use it

This example should run directly in your web browser.

- Wait until webR is initialized and the packages are installed (this may take
  a moment on first load).
- Press the run button of the code cell, or modify the code first and then run
  it to explore the model.
  


```{webr-r}
#|  context: interactive
#|  autorun: false
#|  label: Lorenz
#|  fig-height: 10
#|  fig-width: 10

library(deSolve)
library(scatterplot3d)

## Chaos in the atmosphere
Lorenz <- function(t, state, parameters) {
  with(as.list(c(state, parameters)), {
    dX <-  a * X + Y * Z
    dY <-  b * (Y - Z)
    dZ <- -X * Y + c * Y - Z
    list(c(dX, dY, dZ))
  })
}

parameters <- c(a = -8/3, b = -10, c = 28)
state      <- c(X = 1, Y = 1, Z = 1)
times      <- seq(0, 100, by = 0.01)

out <- ode(y = state, times = times, func = Lorenz, parms = parameters)

plot(out)
scatterplot3d(out[,-1], type = "l")
```


## 3. How to compile it

1. Make sure you have the most recent version of [Quarto](https://quarto.org/docs/download/) (>= 1.11.9).
2. Checkout the [source code](https://github.com/tpetzoldt/dynamic-R-models/) and load it into RStudio. 
3. Then open a terminal, make sure you are in the right folder, and install the quarto-webr extension:
```
quarto add coatless/quarto-webr
```
4. then render the Quarto page from the menu or from the terminal with:

```
quarto render index.qmd
```
5. Finally, open it in a compatible browser (e.g. Chrome) or upload it to your favorite web server.

## 4. Further reading

- [webR — official documentation](https://docs.r-wasm.org/webr/latest/):
  how webR works, its communication channels, and how to embed it in web pages.
- [r-wasm package repository](https://repo.r-wasm.org/):
  pre-compiled WebAssembly binaries of R packages, including **deSolve**.
- [quarto-webr extension](https://github.com/coatless/quarto-webr):
  the community-developed Quarto extension used in this example, which enables
  interactive webR code cells in HTML documents, Revealjs slides, websites,
  blogs, and books.
- [Making your first webR-powered Quarto document](https://quarto-webr.thecoatlessprofessor.com/qwebr-first-steps.html):
  a step-by-step tutorial covering installation, rendering, and document-level
  customizations of the quarto-webr extension.
- [deSolve on CRAN](https://cran.r-project.org/package=deSolve):
  documentation and vignettes of the deSolve package for numerical solving of
  differential equations.
